confirmed.statement: S1 (Experiment 1): 260 complete MTurk responses, 27 removed for non-sensical responses, 233 people analyzed. The Results give n = 233, and the t-tests have 231 df (233 minus 2 arms).
confirmed.quote: We collected 260 complete responses from MTurk. After we removed 27 participants who provided non-sensical responses, 233 participants (mean age, 42.29 years; 52% female) were retained for analysis.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (journal p. 1911), Methods, Experiment 1; PDF p. 2 (journal p. 1907), Results, Experiment 1; PDF p. 5, Table 1

confirmed.statement: S2 (Experiment 2A): preregistered target 300, 298 complete responses, 6 non-sensical and 1 failed attention check removed, 291 people analyzed. F2,288 and t288 equal 291 minus 3 arms.
confirmed.quote: removing six participants who provided non-sensical responses and one participant who failed the attention check. This resulted in a final sample of 291 participants
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-7 (journal pp. 1911-1912), Methods, Experiment 2A; PDF p. 2 (journal p. 1907), Results, Experiment 2A

confirmed.statement: S3 (Experiment 2B): data collection stopped at 200 Prolific responses that passed the attention check and were sensical, plus 100 unedited ChatGPT-3.5 responses with no participant. The Results give n = 200 participants. F2,297 implies 300 observations: 200 people plus 100 ChatGPT outputs.
confirmed.quote: We concluded data collection upon reaching our target of 200 responses (mean age, 41.68 years; 52% female) from Prolific and 100 responses from ChatGPT-3.5.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1912), Methods, Experiment 2B; PDF p. 3 (journal p. 1908), Results, Experiment 2B

confirmed.statement: S4 (Experiment 3): 208 complete MTurk responses, 1 non-sensical and 13 failed attention checks removed, 194 people analyzed. t192 equals 194 minus 2 arms.
confirmed.quote: We collected 208 complete responses from MTurk. After we removed 1 participant who provided non-sensical responses and 13 participants who failed the attention check, 194 participants
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1912), Methods, Experiment 3; PDF p. 3 (journal p. 1908), Results, Experiment 3

confirmed.statement: S5 (Experiment 4): preregistered target 400, survey capped at 405, 405 complete responses, 5 non-sensical removed, 400 people analyzed. F1,396 and t396 equal 400 minus 4 cells.
confirmed.quote: We received 405 complete responses. We then applied the preregistered exclusion criteria, removing five participants who provided non-sensical responses. This resulted in the intended sample of 400 participants
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1912), Methods, Experiment 4; PDF p. 4 (journal p. 1909), Results, Experiment 4

confirmed.statement: S6 (Experiment 5): preregistered target 400, 394 complete responses, 8 non-sensical and 3 failed attention checks removed, 383 people analyzed. F1,379 and t379 equal 383 minus 4 cells.
confirmed.quote: removing eight participants who provided non-sensical responses and three participants who failed the attention check. This resulted in a final sample of 383 participants
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1913), Methods, Experiment 5; PDF pp. 4-5 (journal pp. 1909-1910), Results, Experiment 5

confirmed.statement: The Reporting Summary's exclusion counts (27, 7, 14, 5 and 11; none given for 2B) and its clicked/finished counts (1021/260, 395/298, 356/216, 479/208, 542/405, 554/394) match the form's exclusions fields for all six studies.
confirmed.quote: This resulted in removing 27 participants in Experiment 1, 7 in Experiment 2A, 14 in Experiment 3, 5 in Experiment 4, and 11 in Experiment 5.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Reporting Summary, Data exclusions and Non-participation

confirmed.statement: No experiment prints a count at assignment. People who did not finish were dropped from the dataset, and the PDF does not say how many of them had been randomized, so participants.n_randomized = null is right in every study.
confirmed.quote: Participants who declined consent or did not complete the study to the end were dropped from the dataset.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Reporting Summary, Non-participation and Randomization; PDF pp. 6-8, Methods

confirmed.statement: No arm or cell count is printed: Table 1 has no n column, the Results and Methods give study totals only, and the authors ticked n/a for the per-group sample-size item. Every arms[].n_randomized and arms[].n_analyzed = null is right.
confirmed.quote: The exact sample size (n) for each experimental group/condition, given as a discrete number and unit of measurement
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5 (journal p. 1910), Table 1; PDF p. 10, Reporting Summary, Statistics checklist (n/a box ticked)

confirmed.statement: The counts are people, not ideas or ratings. Each total carries a mean age and percent female. Experiment 1 participants entered about 1.69 ideas each, averaged to one score per participant. Judge panels (331, 232, 241, 158, 321 and 310 lay judges, plus three experts) are not counted as participants.
confirmed.quote: As participants could have submitted more than one idea, the scores for each idea were aggregated to calculate an average creativity score for each participant
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6 (journal p. 1911), Methods, Experiment 1, Creativity ratings; judge counts at PDF pp. 2-4 and 6-8

confirmed.statement: In Experiment 2B the 100 ChatGPT-only responses involve no participant. The form leaves that arm's people counts null (form-spec rule 5) and counts the responses only in n_units (300 in S3-O4 and S3-O5).
confirmed.quote: For the ChatGPT-only condition, we directly entered the same prompt given to the participants into ChatGPT-3.5, obtaining 100 responses by entering the prompt 100 times.

confirmed.statement: Each experiment alone has at least 194 people analyzed (Experiment 3 is the smallest), so criterion 2 (50 or more people) holds study by study.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-8 (journal pp. 1911-1913), Methods, Experiments 1 to 5

confirmed.statement: Other paper: Meincke, Nave and Terwiesch (2025; candidate c015) reanalyze Lee and Chung's OSF data for all six experiments (their Fig. 1 has panels for Experiments 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4 and 5), so the form's paper-level overlap is right. The c010 PDF cannot name c015 because it came out first.
confirmed.quote: The data reported in this paper were collected by Lee and Chung and are available via OSF at https://osf.io/rzn87
confirmed.locator: c015 PDF p. 3 (journal p. 1109), Data availability; c015 PDF p. 1 (journal p. 1107), right column; c015 Fig. 1, PDF p. 2

confirmed.statement: c015 prints one arm-level number that the c010 PDF lacks: 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas in Experiment 2A, one idea per participant. Null stays right in this form, which records only what the c010 PDF states.
confirmed.quote: in Lee and Chung’s experiment 2A, 20 out of 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas included the word ‘sprinkler’
confirmed.locator: c015 PDF p. 1 (journal p. 1107), right column

confirmed.statement: Within the paper, the PDF does not say whether one person could take part in more than one experiment. Each experiment reports its own recruitment, completion counts and dates (1 and 3 on MTurk in February and May 2023; 2A, 4 and 5 on Prolific in June and July 2023; 2B on Prolific in January 2024). The form makes no claim either way. Each design is between-participants, so overlap across experiments could not push any study below 50.
confirmed.quote: Researchers had no control over selecting participants other than specifying data-quality restrictions.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Reporting Summary, Sampling strategy and Timing

confirmed.statement: S3 who and ai_tool: the 98.04 percent GPT-3.5 figure matches the text. The text gives no denominator, and 98.04 percent of 200 is 196.08 people, so it is a share of a subset (it equals 50/51 or 100/102), not of all 200 analyzed. No count depends on it.
confirmed.quote: Indeed, this was confirmed in our main experiment; the majority of participants (98.04%) reported having used GPT-3.5.

confirmed.statement: All six participants.quote strings and their locators in the form match the PDF word for word.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 6-8 (journal pp. 1911-1913), Methods; PDF pp. 2-4, Results

summary: Every people count in the form matches the PDF: 233, 291, 200, 194, 400 and 383 people analyzed in Experiments 1, 2A, 2B, 3, 4 and 5, with exclusions and completion counts that reconcile with the Reporting Summary, null randomized and arm counts because the paper prints neither, the 100 ChatGPT-only outputs kept out of the people count, and every experiment alone far above 50 people. Caveats that change no count: the PDF never says whether one person could join more than one experiment, the Experiment 2B share of 98.04 percent GPT-3.5 users cannot be a share of all 200 people, and, outside this lens, source.version wrongly says the markdown omits the references and Reporting Summary (md lines 271-523 hold them).
